criteria_results.text: Every dedicated tool screen handles loading, empty, secret-free offline cache, forbidden, expired-auth, and retryable server error with accessible Dynamic Type and dark-mode-safe UI.
criteria_results.notes: The focused issue-1173-c11 contract passed, and the native development client rendered Webhooks correctly at the normal text size. On the iOS 18.3 iPhone SE simulator in dark appearance at accessibility-extra-extra-extra-large, the first Webhook card's content outgrew its measured scroll extent: action controls were only partially visible and no further scroll exposed them.

process_issues.description: The first Xcode build did not inherit Expo's development/E2E environment and correctly stopped when app.config.ts treated the build as production without release OAuth configuration.
process_issues.detected_by: XcodeBuildMCP build log showed NODE_ENV absent and EXPO_PUBLIC_GOOGLE_MOBILE_CLIENT_ID required; passing NODE_ENV, EXPO_APP_VARIANT, and E2E values as explicit build settings produced a successful rebuild.

issues.description: The recovered aggregate run reached native smoke before its final verification-gate and project-state-updater passes. Those steps remain required after the corrective implementation and must not be treated as complete by this postmortem.
issues.detected_by: Transcript and active roadmap plan inspection.

failure_output: Native iOS 18.3 iPhone SE, dark appearance, accessibility-extra-extra-extra-large: Webhook content visually overflows its measured scroll extent and Copy/Rotate/Delete controls cannot all be reached.
suggested_follow_up: Add a native maximum-Dynamic-Type Webhooks layout contract/evidence check and make expanded card content contribute its full wrapped height to the enclosing scroll view.
